Import iSNV data from tabular files

Source: R/import-table.R
readWithinHostTable.Rd

Reads pre-computed iSNV data from TSV or CSV files and constructs a WithinHostExperiment.

Usage

readWithinHostTable(files, format = c("ivar", "generic"), colData = NULL)

Arguments

files

Character vector. Paths to files (one per sample).

format

Character. "ivar" for iVar TSV output (columns: REGION, POS, REF, ALT, REF_DP, ALT_DP, ALT_FREQ, TOTAL_DP, ...), or "generic" for CSV with columns: chrom, pos, ref, alt, aaf, depth.

colData

DataFrame (optional). Sample metadata with sample_id. If NULL, sample IDs are derived from file basenames.

Value

A WithinHostExperiment.

Details

Only the columns named under format are read.

iVar's PASS column, the outcome of its own test of each call, is not read, so a row with PASS FALSE is imported as a call, and flagISNV judges it by its depth, frequency and read-count thresholds alone. To drop such rows, remove them from the file first, reading every column as text so that the file is written back unchanged:


calls <- read.delim(path, colClasses = "character")
passed <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
write.table(calls[calls$PASS == "TRUE", ], passed, sep = "\t",
    quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
whe <- readWithinHostTable(passed, format = "ivar")

iVar's per-strand counts (REF_RV, ALT_RV) are not imported. The strand-bias step of flagISNV() runs only when the assays fwdAltCount and revAltCount are present, so on an imported object it is skipped and leaves no qcLog row, although qcFilters() records the filter's maxStrandBias; flagStrandBiasSCI stops for want of those assays.

Insertions and deletions are imported as rows of width 1 at their position, with the caller's allele notation (iVar writes +TTG for an insertion and -T for a deletion), and nothing tells them apart from substitutions: they pass flagISNV() like any other call and enter the diversity statistics. A VCF read by readWithinHost writes the same one-base deletion as, for instance, AT to A, so the two routes do not match it by allele. To keep substitutions only, subset to rows whose ref and alt are one base each:


rr <- SummarizedExperiment::rowRanges(whe)
whe <- whe[nchar(rr$ref) == 1L & nchar(rr$alt) == 1L, ]

Examples

tsv <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor_ivar.tsv",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
whe <- readWithinHostTable(tsv, format = "ivar")
whe
#> WithinHostExperiment with 15 variant sites and 1 samples
#>   assays(5): altFreq, totalDepth, refCount, altCount, qcPass
#>   qcLog: 0 filtering step(s)
#>   transmission pairs: 0 

## Only the rows iVar passed
calls <- read.delim(tsv, colClasses = "character")
passed <- tempfile(fileext = ".tsv")
write.table(calls[calls$PASS == "TRUE", ], passed, sep = "\t",
    quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
readWithinHostTable(passed, format = "ivar")
#> WithinHostExperiment with 15 variant sites and 1 samples
#>   assays(5): altFreq, totalDepth, refCount, altCount, qcPass
#>   qcLog: 0 filtering step(s)
#>   transmission pairs: 0
